newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end moderately up, gains slow.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end moderately up, gains slow.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended moderately higher on Tuesday as players covered their positions after four days of declines.
The dollar's firmer tone against the yen contributed to some buying of blue chip stocks in the underlying cash market.
But dealers said the market was still confined to a 300-points range with resistance expected near the key 20,000 points level.
The lead Nikkei 225 September contract finished 125 points higher at 19,885 after hitting a peak at 19,970.

"We tried to test the morning high again but a lot of arbitrageurs wanted to sell there. Towards the close, some houses were trying to buy to cover their positions," a trader at a Japanese futures house said.
He said the market was likely to remain well supported above 19,650 as people who had gone short would buy back around that level.
"It seems people don't have much confidence in the Japanese economy. If they did, the Nikkei would be above 20,000," he added.

Taiwan MSCI futures ended lower in line with Taipei stocks after the central bank issued T$11 billion negotiable certificates of deposit to mop up excess liquidity on Monday, The most active July contract ended down 3.5 points at 395.5 on 1,240 lots.
